messages:
Connor O'Brien: Kicking off coordination for the SDK parity releases (py/ts/go). Need to lock: version numbers, changelog wording, release order + timing, and doc updates. Goal is same-day release if we can.

Connor O'Brien: Proposed target window: Thu 2026-02-19 10:00–13:00 PT. Please reply with (a) your SDK version bump plan (b) whether you need beta tag first.

Monica Patel: +1 same-day. Let’s make sure migration notes + docs PR are live before stable tags. Also want consistent language across changelogs: “Standardized retries/timeouts/auth resolution + improved streaming error surfacing.”

Ibrahim Khan: From parity standpoint we should ship stable once conformance suite green in all three repos on main + gateway changes are deployed (Retry-After + request_id propagation).

ReleaseBot: reminder: release cutoffs for Thu are 09:00 PT for anything needing infra help. :information_source:

Sabrina James: Python: plan to cut redwood-sdk-python v1.12.0 (minor) from current v1.11.3. No public API surface breaking, but default retry/timeout behavior changes could be “behavioral breaking” for some. We added opt-out knobs + clear docs.

Sabrina James: Also want to include deprecation note: `REDWOOD_API_KEY` (legacy) -> prefer `REDWOOD_API_TOKEN` (new standard). We still support both with precedence rules.

Dana Lo: TS: currently 1.18.2. Planning 1.19.0. Includes retry middleware refactor + AbortController timeout plumbing. We’re emitting typed errors now (request_id, status_code, retryable) and deprecating old env var names with console.warn once.

Mateusz Zielinski: Go: currently v0.9.6. Planning v0.10.0 (minor, still <1.0). Includes Retry-After + backoff jitter alignment, context cancellation fixes, and streaming error types. Also adds conformance harness.

Connor O'Brien: Great. For comms: are we comfortable calling these “standardized defaults” in release notes? PM was nervous about sounding like we changed semantics too much.

Ibrahim Khan: Suggest phrasing: “Aligned defaults + added configuration consistency across languages.” Then list the concrete changes + link to migration guide. Avoid “breaking.”

Dev Patel: From Support: please explicitly call out: 429 handling respects Retry-After now, request_id included in exceptions, and streaming disconnects raise a typed error. These map directly to top tickets.

Elliot Price: Docs side: we have redwood-docs PR ready but it references final version numbers. Can we lock versions today? Also need to coordinate quickstarts repo PR merge.

Wei Chen: +1. For docs, I need final option names (esp timeout fields) to match across all three snippets. Last time we had `timeoutMs` vs `timeout_ms` mismatch.

Dana Lo: TS uses `timeoutMs` for user-facing option, but we can document as `timeoutMs` in TS and `timeout_ms` in py/go. The key is same semantics + same defaults.

Ibrahim Khan: Semantics per ADR: overall timeout is primary. If SDK supports connect/read, expose but map to overall. Default overall: 60s non-streaming, streaming has idle/read timeout 5m with heartbeat handling.

Sabrina James: Python exposes `timeout` (overall seconds) and `connect_timeout`/`read_timeout` advanced. Defaults: overall=60s, connect=10s, read=60s. Streaming read idle=300s.

Mateusz Zielinski: Go: `Timeout` overall in client options, plus per-request context deadline recommended. Streaming uses context; we added explicit read deadline to detect half-open connections.

Connor O'Brien: Version lock proposal:
- Python: 1.12.0
- TS: 1.19.0
- Go: 0.10.0
Docs/quickstarts should reference these.

Monica Patel: Works for me.

Sahana Iyer: CI note: conformance runs are green in py and go; TS is failing one fixture around streaming 429 path (it retries once even though it should not retry mid-stream). Dana, can you confirm fix ETA?

Dana Lo: Yep, I see it. It’s the fetch stream wrapper classifying the first chunk incorrectly. Patch is up locally; I can get it merged within ~2 hours.

Ibrahim Khan: Important: streaming retry policy is “do not auto-retry after any bytes delivered.” We can retry only if connection fails before first byte + request is idempotent (and we still recommend user-managed retry).

Connor O'Brien: Release ordering suggestion:
1) Merge + tag gateway PRs already deployed? (Ethan said rollout complete by Wed EOD)
2) Merge conformance fixes in TS
3) Merge docs + quickstarts
4) Tag SDKs within same hour
Agree?

Wei Chen: For docs, we can merge once versions are confirmed and option names finalized. Need a heads up when TS conformance green so we can flip docs to “Released” vs “Beta.”

Elliot Price: Also need changelog bullets from each owner by EOD so we can keep consistent tone.

Sabrina James: Python changelog draft bullets:
- Standardized retry policy (429/5xx/network) with exponential backoff + jitter; respects Retry-After.
- Standardized timeout model; streaming idle timeout defaults + clearer cancellation.
- Auth env var precedence aligned; improved secret redaction in errors.
- Errors now include request_id when available.

Mateusz Zielinski: Go changelog draft bullets:
- Added Retry-After support + jittered exponential backoff; retryable classification aligned.
- Context cancellation consistently aborts HTTP + streaming reads.
- Streaming errors include request_id/status_code; guidance on safe retries.
- Added conformance test harness integration.

Dana Lo: TS changelog draft bullets:
- Unified retry middleware and typed error shapes (request_id, retryable, status_code).
- Timeouts standardized; AbortController wired for streaming/non-streaming.
- Retry-After parsing supports seconds + HTTP-date.
- Env var names aligned; deprecation warnings for old names.

Dev Patel: Please add explicit note: “SDKs will not retry on 4xx other than 408/409/429” (we keep getting tickets about 400 retries).

Ibrahim Khan: +1. Also call out 409 retry requires idempotency guidance (for non-GET). But defaults: 409 retryable only for specific error codes (conflict on idempotent requests). If we can’t guarantee, keep 409 off by default.

Monica Patel: Per standard, default retryable status codes are 408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504 + network errors. 409 is opt-in. Let’s keep changelog aligned to that.

Connor O'Brien: Good catch — update your changelog bullets to reflect that (no mention of 409 default). Dev/Support text can say “4xx not retried except 408/429.”

Sahana Iyer: FYI once TS fix merges, conformance suite will run on tag workflow too. Please don’t cut tags until we see green on the release commit.

Connor O'Brien: Timing plan (tentative):
- Thu 10:00 PT: merge docs + quickstarts (after SDKs green)
- Thu 11:00 PT: cut SDK tags (py/ts/go) back-to-back
- Thu 11:30 PT: publish release notes + #announcements message w/ migration link
Roll back criteria: if retry rate spikes >2x baseline or 429 storm indicators on dashboards.

Elliot Price: Works. I’ll prep the release note template + links.

Wei Chen: I’ll update migration page with final versions once tags exist; until then it’ll reference “next release.”

Dana Lo: TS conformance fix is up in a PR now; will post link in #devex when merged. ETA 1–2 hrs.

Connor O'Brien: Perfect. Please drop final changelog text in this thread when ready. I’ll coordinate tagging commands + checklists. :thumbsup:

ReleaseBot: scheduled reminder created for 2026-02-19 10:00 PT: “SDK parity releases: merge docs/quickstarts, tag py/ts/go, announce.”
